strengths: The task addresses a meaningful gap between audio-visual semantic segmentation and video instance segmentation: distinguishing individual sounding objects while maintaining identities and predicting their sounding intervals. AVISeg is a substantial contribution, with 926 videos averaging 61.4 seconds, 94,074 instance masks, and 26 categories. Its inclusion of silent and simultaneous-source frames makes it useful for studying sound-conditioned visual understanding.

The main comparison provides consistent evidence of baseline effectiveness. Under the reported common ResNet-50 backbone and 48,000-iteration training budget, AVISM achieves 61.73 HOTA and 40.57 mAP, compared with VITA's 57.48/36.25 and COMBO's 57.39/37.84 (Table 2). Improvements in both detection and association support the contribution independently of the proposed FSLA metric.

The ablations substantiate the audio-fusion design. Adding frame-level fusion raises HOTA from 57.48 to 59.59, and adding video-level fusion further increases it to 61.73 (Table 4). The similarity-loss ablation and backbone/pretraining experiments provide additional evidence about which components contribute to performance.

The manuscript clearly illustrates the task and architecture, reports useful implementation settings, and supplies qualitative comparisons and explicit failure cases involving similar sounding instances. The substantial benchmark contribution and gains on established metrics provide a stronger case for acceptance despite the reservations below.
weaknesses: FSLA has a material specification and reproducibility problem. Algorithm 1 counts silent frames as correct without checking predictions, initializes counters outside the IoU-threshold loop without resetting them, and omits explicit checks that predicted and ground-truth instance counts agree and every object is correctly matched. Its aggregation also does not implement the stated class averaging. The algorithm cannot reproduce the reported metric as written, although this does not establish that the experimental implementation is wrong. Separately, the assertion that nonsounding predictions cannot reduce mAP is too categorical: their effect depends on confidence ranking.

The large-model conclusions are confounded by restrictive adaptations. Supplementary Section E merges same-category masks into one identity for Sam4AVS and BuboGPT and treats each category as one instance for AL-Ref-SAM 2. Sam4AVS additionally receives only the top-ranked audio class despite the prevalence of multiple sources. These design choices directly prevent successful same-category instance separation, so Table 3 supports conclusions about these particular pipelines more strongly than general claims about large models' instance reasoning.

The reliability of sound-source attribution is insufficiently characterized for a dataset-centered contribution. Section 4 describes SAM-assisted masks and repeated manual review, but provides no quantitative annotation audit or agreement measure and little guidance on resolving ambiguous concurrent sounds from similar objects. The rule for assigning sound activity within each one-second interval is also unclear. These omissions limit assessment of the ground truth for the task's hardest cases.

Evidence for the strongest temporal and practical claims remains limited. Evaluation uses 1 FPS, and 539 of 926 videos belong to the music scenario. Aggregate scores do not isolate same-category competing sources, sound onsets/offsets, or performance as sequence length increases. Table 5 reports maximum processable frames but lacks matched runtime and memory comparisons with competing methods. Consequently, fine temporal perception, broader generalization, and comparative efficiency are only partially established.

Methodological originality is modest: object-token condensation, shifted-window temporal processing, video queries, and similarity supervision largely follow Mask2Former/VITA, with audio fusion providing the principal adaptation. Some reproduction details remain unspecified, including training clip length/temporal sampling and fusion-layer counts. These reservations limit the algorithmic contribution without negating the value of the task and benchmark.
